DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle. Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph 1 4 CIAN OPINION NO. ATTY. ANTHONY C. NUYDA Regional Director DILG-Region V Rizal St., Legazpi City Dear RD Nuyda: S. 2t)LQ This pertains to your Memorandum dated 14 October 2019, requesting the Central Office's legal opinion on the alleged double compensation by a member of Sangguniang Barangay who is an active Citizen Armed Force Geographical Units (CAFGU) personnel at the same time. Perusal of the documents submitted to the Department, it appears that the surname of the subject person as reflected in the letter dated 28 May 2019 of Major General Fernando T. Trinidad is different from the surname reflected in the Certification with reference no. 221B-D6 issued by Captain Alberto E. Sellingan. Further, in letter dated 28 May 2019, it informed the Department that Mr. Jimmy Del Monte is not a Citizen Armed Force Geographical Unit (CAFGU) member of Bicol Region, while in the Certification, it certified that Jimmy R. Belmonte is a bonafide member of 2nd Platoon 3rd Camarines Sur CAFGU Active Auxiliary (CAA) unit. Nevertheless, for purposes of addressing the concern, the Department will assume that Jimmy Del Monte and Jimmy Belmonte is one and the same person, and is a bonafide member of CAFGU. Foremost, we find it imperative to cite the following provisions of the Philippine Constitution and RA No. 7160, or Local Government Code, viz: Sections 7 and 8t Article IX(B) of the Philippine Constitution "SECTION 7. No elective official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure. Unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his position, no appointive official shall hold any other office or employment in the Government or any subdivision, agency or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries.

SECTION 8. No elective or appointive public officer or employee shall receive additional, double, or indirect compensation, unless specifically authorized by law, nor accept without the consent of the Congress, any present, emolument, office, or title of any kind from any foreign government. Pensions or gratuities shall not be considered as additional, double, or indirect compensation. " Section 95 of the Local Government Code "SECTION 95. Additional or Double Compensation. - No elective or appointive local official or employee shall receive additional, double, or indirect compensation, unless specifically authorized by law, nor accept without the consent of Congress, any present, emoluments, office, or title of any kind from any foreign government. Pensions or gratuities shall not be considered as additional, double, or indirect compensation. " From the afore-quoted provisions, an elective official is generally ineligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure, and should not receive additional, double, or compensation, unless specifically authorized by law. However, Section 62 of RA No. 7077, otherwise known as the Citizen Armed Forces of the Philippines Reservist Act allows the President to call upon the reservists in the concerned localities to volunteer their services, referred to as the Military Auxiliary Service, where, elected/appointed local government officials are expected to perform their duties and responsibilities in their respective peace and order council levels or similar organizations efficiently and effectively to enhance a total integrated system approach against threats to national security. More importantly, no less than the Constitution, permitted the Government to call upon the people to defend the State and, in the fulfillment thereof, all citizens may be required, under conditions provided by law, to render personal military, or civil servicel. As regards the subsistence allowance received by them, Section 65 of RA No. 7077 is enlightening, it states: "Section 64. Status of Reservists on Auxiliary Service. - A reservist performing auxiliary service shall not receive payment but shall be entitled to receive allowances and burial benefits as provided by law. With his consent, a reservist may continue to render such services without Section 4, Article II of the 1987 Philippine Constitution

receiving the allowances due him. A reservist serving military auxiliary services is subject to military law; whereas, a reservist serving civil auxiliary service is not. " (Emphasis supplied) Accordingly, the Department is of the view that a local elective official's membership in CAFGU is allowed and the subsistence allowance received by them is authorized by law. We hope that we have sufficiently addressed your concern. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secreta IN B. DINO dersecretary LS/90
